title: Fast Adaptive Kernel Intensity Estimation for Spatio‐Temporal Point Processes via Bandwidth Quantile Partitioning
content:
ABSTRACT

In spatio-temporal point pattern analysis, one of the main statistical objectives is to estimate the first-order intensity function, that is, the expected number of points per unit area and unit time. This estimation is usually carried out nonparametrically using kernel functions, and one of the most frequent challenges is selecting kernel bandwidths prior to estimation. This work presents an intensity estimation mechanism in which the spatial and temporal bandwidths change at each data point in a spatio-temporal point pattern. This class of estimators is called adaptive estimators, and although they have been studied in spatial settings, little has been said about them in the spatio-temporal context. We define an adaptive intensity estimator in the spatio-temporal setting and extend a bandwidth-quantile-based partitioning technique to enable fast estimation. We demonstrate through simulation that the partition estimator closely approximates the direct adaptive estimator while substantially reducing computation time. Finally, we apply our method to estimate the spatio-temporal intensity of fires in the Amazonia basin.

Jonatan A. González,
